title: Night Wings: The True Story of a Little Brown Bat
summary: In this true story, a tiny little brown bat wakes at dusk, flies on wings that are really hands, finds moths in the dark with echoes, and snuggles into a quiet cave to hibernate for the winter.
character: the little brown bat, ONE small realistic little brown bat with glossy warm cocoa-brown fur, a slightly paler tan belly, thin dark brown leathery wings stretched between long slender finger bones, small rounded dark brown ears, a short dark brown snout and tiny shiny black eyes, gentle and sweet-looking

cover.text: Night Wings: The True Story of a Little Brown Bat.
cover.scene: The little brown bat flies toward the viewer with her wings spread wide, showing the long finger bones in her wings, over a calm autumn pond at dusk; golden and orange autumn trees and an old red wooden barn far behind; two small pale moths fluttering nearby; a deep blue and violet dusk sky with the first few stars. Characters in this picture: only ONE bat and two tiny moths

pages.text: When the sun slips down behind the hills on an autumn evening, a little brown bat begins to wake up. She has spent the whole day resting upside down in a dark, cozy corner of an old wooden barn. She is very small. In fact, she weighs about as much as three pennies!
pages.scene: Inside an old wooden barn, seen from a little distance: a low wooden beam runs across the picture at about 60 percent height, and the little brown bat hangs upside down by her toes from it, just waking, eyes half open; a few hay bales on the floor below her; warm sunset light glows on the hay. Characters in this picture: only ONE bat
pages.background: plain smooth flat dusky-brown upper barn wall in ONE even tone with no boards, no planks, no lines, no vignette and no shading changes

pages.text: Hanging upside down might look tricky, but for a bat it is easy. Special cords in her feet hold her toes tightly closed, so she can rest without even trying. Bats sleep about twenty hours a day! Now she stretches her wings, yawns a tiny yawn, and combs her soft fur clean, just like a cat.
pages.scene: Seen from a little distance: a low wooden beam runs across the picture at about 60 percent height, and the little brown bat hangs upside down by her tiny clawed toes from it, stretching one wing out wide and yawning a tiny yawn; soft golden light on the hay below. Characters in this picture: only ONE bat
pages.background: plain smooth flat dusky-brown upper barn wall in ONE even tone with no boards, no planks, no lines, no vignette and no shading changes

pages.text: Is a bat a kind of bird? No! A bat is a mammal, just like a dog, a whale, or you. She has soft fur, and when she was a baby, called a pup, she drank her mother's milk. But bats can do something amazing that no other mammal can do. They can truly fly!
pages.scene: Seen from a little distance: a low wooden beam runs across the picture at about 60 percent height, and the little brown bat hangs upside down from it beside a little round window set low in the wall; on the straw floor below, small and far away, ONE sleepy farm dog curled up asleep. Characters in this picture: ONE bat and ONE dog
pages.background: plain smooth flat dusky-brown upper barn wall in ONE even tone with no boards, no planks, no lines, no vignette and no shading changes

pages.text: Look closely at her wings. They are really her hands! A bat's wing has long, thin finger bones with stretchy skin between them, like a kite. The scientific name for bats even means hand-wing. She lets go with her toes, drops into the air, and flap, flap, flap, off she goes!
pages.scene: Low over a dusky meadow, the little brown bat flies with both wings spread wide and flat so the long slender finger bones and thin skin of each wing show clearly, like a natural-history drawing; low grass and a few fallen leaves below. Characters in this picture: only ONE bat
pages.background: smooth violet and peach dusk sky

pages.text: Out she flies into the purple dusk. More little brown bats swoop out of the barn too, zigging and zagging over the meadow. The air is cool and smells of fallen leaves. It is time for breakfast. Yes, breakfast! When you are getting ready for bed, a bat's day is just beginning.
pages.scene: Wide distant view, everything in the bottom 45 percent of the picture: a small old red wooden barn sits low on the horizon in an autumn meadow; the little brown bat flies in the front, clearly visible, with FOUR other tiny little brown bats far behind her swooping out of the barn's open loft door; low orange autumn bushes. Characters in this picture: the little brown bat plus four tiny distant bats
pages.background: smooth deep violet dusk sky fading to peach at the horizon

pages.text: But how can she find tiny bugs in the dark? She calls out with quick, high squeaks, too high for our ears to hear. The sounds bounce off a moth and come back to her as echoes. The echoes tell her where the moth is and which way it is flying. This is called echolocation.
pages.scene: The little brown bat flies low over a dark meadow at night with her mouth slightly open, calling; faint gentle curved ripple lines (sound waves) spread from her toward ONE small pale moth fluttering near some low tall grass; soft moonlit colors. Characters in this picture: ONE bat and ONE moth
pages.background: smooth deep blue night sky with a few tiny faint stars

pages.text: If we could hear her, her calls might go squeak, squeak, squeak, and then faster and faster, squeakity, squeak! Then she scoops up the moth with the skin of her wing and pops it into her mouth. Got it! A little brown bat can catch hundreds of tiny bugs in just one hour.
pages.scene: The little brown bat swoops low over the meadow, curling one wing forward to scoop up ONE small pale moth, her eyes bright and focused; low grass and a few tiny glowing fireflies below. Characters in this picture: ONE bat and ONE moth
pages.background: smooth deep blue night sky with a few tiny faint stars

pages.text: Down by the pond, the air is full of gnats and mosquitoes. She swoops low over the still water and takes a sip while she flies, skimming the surface like a tiny airplane. Then she zooms back up for more bugs. All night she flies and eats, and stops now and then to rest.
pages.scene: The little brown bat skims just above a calm, still pond at night, dipping her chin to sip the water, leaving a tiny ripple trail; cattails low along the far shore; tiny specks of gnats above the water. Characters in this picture: only ONE bat
pages.background: smooth deep blue night sky with a few tiny faint stars, reflected in the calm water

pages.text: Bats are wonderful helpers. By eating so many bugs, little brown bats help farmers and gardens, and that means fewer itchy mosquito bites for us. Far away in warm places, other bats called fruit bats help plants too. They carry pollen from flower to flower, and drop seeds that grow into brand-new trees.
pages.scene: The little brown bat flies low over a moonlit farm garden with rows of small round orange pumpkins, squash leaves and low cabbages, a few tiny moths around her. Characters in this picture: ONE bat and a few tiny moths
pages.background: smooth deep blue night sky with a few tiny faint stars

pages.text: As autumn goes on, the nights grow longer and colder, and there are fewer bugs to catch. So the little brown bat eats and eats, getting a little plumper each night. The extra fat is like a packed lunch she carries inside her body. She will need it soon, because winter is coming.
pages.scene: The little brown bat, now a little plumper and rounder, flies low over a meadow covered in fallen red, orange and brown leaves, with bare low bushes and a light frost on the grass; ONE small moth ahead of her. Characters in this picture: ONE bat and ONE moth
pages.background: smooth cold pale blue and lavender late-autumn evening sky

pages.text: One chilly night, she flies away to a big, quiet cave in the hills. Inside, it is dark and damp and calm. It is not freezing cold, and it is not warm, which is just right. Many other little brown bats have come here too, ready for the long winter.
pages.scene: Wide distant view: a low rocky hillside with a round dark cave opening near the bottom of the picture; the little brown bat flies toward the cave entrance; a few frosty low bushes and rocks. Characters in this picture: only ONE bat
pages.background: smooth deep blue starry night sky with tiny faint stars

pages.text: She hooks her toes onto the rock, wraps her wings around herself like a blanket, and snuggles close to her friends. Then she begins to hibernate. Her body cools down, and her heart, which raced so fast when she flew, slows way, way down. She will sleep almost all winter long.
pages.scene: Inside the calm cave, seen from a little distance: a low rock ledge runs across the picture at about 60 percent height; the little brown bat and FIVE other sleeping little brown bats hang UPSIDE DOWN by their toes from the underside of that ledge, heads pointing down, wings wrapped around them like blankets, eyes closed, snuggled together; tiny sparkling water droplets on the rock. Characters in this picture: the little brown bat plus five other sleeping bats
pages.background: plain smooth flat dark grey-blue cave wall in ONE even tone with no cracks, no vignette and no shading changes

pages.text: Outside, snow falls softly over the hills. Inside the cave, the little brown bat dreams, upside down and cozy. When spring comes and the bugs come back, she will wake up and fly into the evening sky once more. But for now, it is time to sleep. Goodnight, little bat.
pages.scene: Inside the cave, seen from a little distance: the little brown bat hangs UPSIDE DOWN by her toes from the underside of a low rock ledge at about 60 percent height, head pointing down, wings wrapped around her like a blanket, eyes closed, a tiny peaceful smile; beside her, a low round cave opening (entirely in the bottom 45 percent) shows soft snow falling on a snowy hillside under a gentle blue winter night. No symbols or icons in the corners. Characters in this picture: only ONE bat
pages.background: plain smooth flat dark grey-blue cave wall in ONE even tone with no cracks, no vignette and no shading changes

end.text: The end. Goodnight, little bat, and sweet dreams!
